messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: reshape2 doesn't allow quote(var) and .(var)
parts:
reshape2 doesn't seem to allow variable lists quoted with quote(...) or .(...).  Is there some deep reason for this, or is it just a TBD?

> test <- data.frame(a=c(1,2,1,2),b=c(1,1,2,2),v1=11:14,v2=21:24)
> melt(test,c("a","b"))
  a b variable value
1 1 1       v1    11
...                                                                           OK
> melt(test,.(a,b))
Error in .subset(x, j) : invalid subscript type 'list'      <<<<<<< error
> melt(test,quote(a))
Error in as.vector(x, mode) :                                     <<<<<<< error
  cannot coerce type 'symbol' to vector of type 'any'

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: reshape2 doesn't allow quote(var) and .(var)

computation - it just works with existing variables.

parts:
Yes, but it's confusing that some functions take strings and others take symbols (and some take either).

But ddply seems to allow either, though symbols using the .() convention seem to be preferred.

So why shouldn't reshape and melt?  What is the performance hit of as.character(.(a,b,c))?

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: reshape2 doesn't allow quote(var) and .(var)
parts:
> Yes, but it's confusing that some functions take strings and others take
> symbols (and some take either).

Well plyr takes anything (symbols, strings, formula, ...) and ggplot2
is transitioning to the same semantics as plyr. Reshape only accepts
column indexes.

> But ddply seems to allow either, though symbols using the .() convention
> seem to be preferred.
> So why shouldn't reshape and melt?  What is the performance hit
> of as.character(.(a,b,c))?

It's more the semantics - reshape would have to evaluate the variables
if you had .(a + b, round(c)) etc.

Hadley
